_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC §4
protagonist: Priya Kessler, 3-D scanning / photogrammetry technician at a small VFX digitization studio

deliverables.text: A scan-scale note in scientific notation: real vertex/triangle counts for the Stanford scans in Appendix A written in scientific notation, plus what percent of total scanned vertices belong to the suspect mirrored pass.
A congruence-or-similarity audit: marker-to-marker distances within the expected set and the actual set from Appendix B, and a justified decision of congruent, similar, or neither.

A reflection test and quadrant map: plot expected/actual marker coordinates, label each point's quadrant, and compare the suspect marker's actual position to its position under a reflection across the rig's y-axis.

A translation check: solve a system of two equations for the (Δx, Δy) offset from the two trustworthy markers, then predict the suspect marker's position under a pure translation and compare to its actual position.
A registration-error-per-minute comparison for Option A vs. Option B, plus a deadline check on whether Option B's manual pass fits before end of day.

balance.argument_a: Ship As Converged costs 0 additional technician minutes (Appendix C) and the rig's own accepted convergence signal -- a reported error of 0.40mm -- is the studio's normal basis for export; 2 of the 3 known markers land exactly where expected, and the face-value ratio of 0.004444 mm/min beats Option B's 0.004472 mm/min by 0.61%.
balance.argument_b: Marker 3's actual position is 160.65mm away from its predicted pure-translation position -- consistent with a reflection, not a rotation or translation -- a documented failure mode automatic alignment solvers cannot self-detect, so the rig's self-reported 0.40mm cannot be trusted; the studio's $8,500 re-shoot cost dwarfs the 33 extra technician minutes (3 markers x 7 min + 12 min, Appendix C) Option B spends, which fits inside the 50-minute deadline window with 17 minutes to spare.
balance.margin_basis: Total technician minutes on the job (90 min already spent, common to both options) plus each option's own minutes: Option A adds 0 (ships as-is); Option B adds 3x7=21 min (MA2, re-register 3 markers) + 12 min (MA3, re-export/re-check) = 33, for 123 total. Face-value ratio A = rig's own self-reported error 0.40mm (MA4) / 90 min = 0.004444 mm/min. Face-value ratio B = manual-correction residual 0.55mm (MA5) / 123 min = 0.004472 mm/min. Margin between these two face-value ratios = 0.61% -- razor-thin, Robotics-Engineering-exemplar style, and exactly the trap: Option A looks marginally better ONLY by trusting the rig's unverified 0.40mm. Once D2-D4's real marker geometry is used instead (Marker 3's actual position vs. its predicted pure-translation position, from the two trustworthy markers' real Delta=(+3.00,+2.00)cm offset), Option A's TRUE leftover error is ~160.65mm (a reflection, not noise) -- true ratio 160.65/90=1.785 mm/min, ~400x worse than Option B's 0.0045, and far above Appendix D's 1.0mm tolerance (MA1) where Option B's 0.55mm passes comfortably. Appendix C's deadline check: converged at 4:40pm, deadline 5:30pm (50 min window), Option B needs 33 min -- fits with 17 min to spare.
balance.true_reveal_ratio_note: Using the D2-D4-derived real error (160.65mm) instead of the rig's self-reported 0.40mm, Option A's true ratio is ~1.785 mm/min vs Option B's 0.00447 mm/min -- the reveal that the naive 0.61% margin was built entirely on an unverified number. Facilitator-only; not written into case.md.

modeling_assumptions.basis: No single public source states a general VFX-prop-scan registration tolerance; published scan-to-CAD tolerances range ~0.005-0.03mm (precision optical-metrology parts, CMM-inspected) to ~0.8mm (formed sheet-metal scan-to-CAD) [S4]. 1.0mm sits at the loose end of that real range, appropriate to a VFX prop replica.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Below ~0.55mm, even Option B's corrected residual (MA5) fails client acceptance. Above ~0.55mm, Option B passes comfortably; Option A's real marker-derived error (~160.65mm) fails at any plausible tolerance.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Technician time to manually re-register one marker
modeling_assumptions.basis: Manual marker placement is a documented per-point, multi-photo task in professional photogrammetry pipelines [S3]; no public source gives a minutes-per-marker figure for any studio.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Feeds Option B's total minutes (3x7=21 of the 33 task-specific minutes, 123 total). At 15 min/marker instead, Option B's total rises to 147 minutes, straining the Appendix C deadline window.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Technician time to re-export and re-run the client's registration check
modeling_assumptions.basis: Same basis as MA2 -- a disclosed estimate for a real task, not a published figure.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Directly tightens the Appendix C deadline check (50-minute window) before the ratio comparison even matters.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Stated scenario value representing a plausible, misleadingly low self-report -- the central trap of the case.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Option A's face-value D5 ratio depends entirely on this single unverified number; the whole margin_pct (0.61%) rests on it being trusted at face value.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Manual-correction residual error after Option B
modeling_assumptions.basis: Stated scenario value for real, small imprecision remaining after careful hand-registration against three ground-truth markers.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Set just above MA4's naive ratio threshold by design; if MA1/MA5 were resized the face-value margin flips.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Documented failure-mode framing as a reflection specifically
modeling_assumptions.basis: S2 documents symmetric/repetitive-pattern alignment failure and marker-based remedy in a real pipeline, but never uses the words mirrored/reflected/converged; this case's reflection framing is a modeling choice suited to the coordinate-plane Challenges (Appendix F), not a verbatim-sourced claim.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: N/A -- framing choice, not a numeric assumption.

sensitivity_note: margin_pct (0.61%) is extremely tight by design and rests entirely on MA4 (rig's self-reported 0.40mm) being trusted; substituting the D2-D4-derived real error (~160.65mm) for MA4 changes Option A's true ratio to ~1.785mm/min, ~400x worse than Option B -- the case's central reveal. MA1 (tolerance) and MA5 (Option B residual) are each other's tripwire (see MA1 sensitivity).

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA2's 7-minutes-per-marker figure is a documented good-faith estimate grounded in the closest public analogue (S3, Agisoft Metashape's own published guide confirming manual marker placement is a genuine per-point, multi-photo task) -- no studio publishes an actual minutes-per-marker figure, so this is a one-time proprietary-estimate exception, not a substitute for real sourcing. Flexing this dial +/-50% flips ONLY the naive, pre-trap face-value D5 ratio a student computes before doing D2-D4 (B wins the face-value ratio by 7.88% at +50%): the case's own D5 metric (mm of error / minutes spent) mathematically rewards MORE minutes at the same fixed 0.55mm Option-B residual, since minutes sits in the denominator. It does NOT move the case's real, trap-independent recommendation: Option A's true ratio (using D2-D4's real 160.65mm error) stays ~1.785 mm/min, ~400x worse than Option B's ~0.0045 mm/min, at every value tested. See sensitivity_model.py for the full sweep.

MA3's 12-minute re-export/re-check estimate is the same kind of documented good-faith estimate as MA2, grounded in the same S3 analogue -- no public source states a re-export/registration-recheck duration for any photogrammetry studio. Flexing this dial +/-50% flips only the naive, pre-trap face-value D5 ratio (B wins the face-value ratio by 4.24% at +50%), for the identical minutes-in-the-denominator reason as MA2. The real, trap-independent recommendation is untouched: Option A's true ratio stays ~400x worse than Option B's across the full sweep, because it rests on the fixed 160.65mm geometric fact from D2-D4, not on either time estimate. See sensitivity_model.py for the full sweep.

sensitivity_disclosure_note: tolerance_mm (MA1) does not flip the face-value winner in either direction (A wins at both +50% and -50%; Option B fails MA1's own tolerance below ~0.55mm, a real disclosed tripwire against MA5, not an instability). Full sweep, from cases/the-point-cloud-match/sensitivity_model.py: tolerance_mm +50% winner=A margin=0.61%; tolerance_mm -50% winner=A margin=0.61%; marker_time_min +50% winner=B margin=7.88% (face-value only); marker_time_min -50% winner=A margin=10.00%; reexport_time_min +50% winner=B margin=4.24% (face-value only); reexport_time_min -50% winner=A margin=5.77%. Real (post-trap) ratios are unaffected by any of the three flexes: Option A ~1.785 mm/min vs Option B ~0.0045 mm/min throughout.
